messages:
sanjay: FYI south-america GPU pool suffered node evictions ~10:12 UTC, traffic shifted to eu-west1 but users report elevated 5xxs. I think DNS failover didn't fully propagate. TTL currently 300s, but many edge caches still resolving to sa1 nodes. Any quick checks?

maria: Can you paste a couple of dig +trace outputs from affected regions? Also which DNS provider/zone are we using for service.example.com?

sanjay: zone is redwood-prod on managed-dns (third-party). dig from a Brazilian resolver:```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +trace service.example.com
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 12345
;; Received 2 records
service.example.com. 300 IN A 34.120.10.5  ; old sa1 IP
;; Received 1 records
;; timing: 455 msec
```

eli: that shows authoritative returned old IP. Did the failover job update the A/ALIAS? Logs from the playbook show success at 10:15:```
2026-03-17T10:15:12Z playbook: create-traffic-shift -> set A -> service.example.com -> 34.200.11.77
2026-03-17T10:15:13Z dns-api: update accepted id=tx-9982
```

maria: could be parent NS/glue issue or our provider not pushing to the global anycast quickly. Can someone run dig @8.8.8.8 service.example.com +short and also check the SOA serial?

eli: results from 8.8.8.8:```
34.120.10.5
```
SOA query:```
service.example.com. 300 IN SOA ns1.managed.example. hostmaster.example.com. 2026031701 7200 3600 1209600 300
```
serial 2026031701 matches post-failover — but A still old. Weird.

opsbot: Incident INC-3124 created (severity: high). Runbook: dns-failover-v2. Assigned: sanjay, maria.

karen: Quick checklist: 1) confirm record change at provider UI/API 2) check parent zone NS glue and TTL 3) check anycast propagation 4) push emergency short TTL/alias if allowed 5) if all else, fail traffic at LB/edge.

maria: Checked provider API: update exists and current A is 34.200.11.77. API returns 200 and the resource shows the new value. So this is a propagation/caching issue. Provider says they respect registrar glue and NS TTLs.

sanjay: I suspect stale glue at the registrar or mismatched NS at the parent. Quick check: whois shows the registered name servers include ns1.managed.example and ns2.managed.example; glue TTL at registrar is 86400. That explains multi-hour cache on some resolvers.

eli: Oof. If glue TTL is high we can't flush upstream caches. Options: 1) create a short-lived ALIAS/CNAME at our apex provider (if supported) pointing to eu-west1 edge hostnames that are on a different name with lower parent TTL; 2) switch traffic routing at CDN level (if we have control) to default to eu-west1; 3) contact registrar to lower glue (slow).

maria: For immediate mitigation I pushed a temporary directional CNAME from failover.service.example.com -> eu-west1-frontend.redwood.net (which we already have low TTL on). Then updated our load balancer to accept requests for service.example.com and redirect. Config snippets:```
# at provider: add CNAME failover.service.example.com -> eu-west1-frontend.redwood.net (TTL 60)
# at edge: add host header rule to accept service.example.com via fallback mapping
```

sanjay: After that we see successful resolves to eu-west IPs from affected resolvers in ~4 minutes. 5xxs start dropping. Good short-term win.

karen: Action items for postmortem: - Pre-stage short-TTL aliases for every critical FQDN before maintenance - Add check for parent/registrar glue TTL in DNS runbook - Add a pre-failover step: verify parent glue TTL <= 3600 or plan ALIAS fallback - Run a canary failover test quarterly

opsbot: Note: Updated runbook dns-failover-v2 at https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/dns-failover-v2 - new step added: check_parent_glue_ttl()

eli: Also recommend monitoring: synthetic resolves from 5 global resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, 209.244.0.3, 185.228.168.9, a regional ISP) and alert if >10% still hit old IP > TTL*2.

maria: Filing follow-up ticket to registrar support to request lower glue TTL and ask if emergency flush possible. Ticket ID: REG-879.

sanjay: Thanks all. Leaving incident open for 1hr to watch. Will add final timeline and root cause once we confirm registrar response. :white_check_mark:
